output.summary: The record year is mostly a commodity price rally: prices rose 36-46%, peers grew revenue 41% without any program, and the cooperative ranks 8th of 23 on revenue and 10th on net savings. The 6% cost-per-bushel gain comes entirely from maintenance cut from $905K to $612K while deferred work orders tripled to $1.26M. Harlan Junction has insurer-critical dust and monitoring findings with a 21 November deadline, and reports go unacted on. The Superintendent's practices are undocumented, with no successor. The expansion proposal has no downside-price margin or debt-service analysis and no staffing or maintenance plan. Fix hazards, start succession and rebuild the financial case before voting.
